# Setting up the SRA Toolkit {#sec-setup}

The **SRA Toolkit** is NCBI's set of command-line programs for SRA data. You
need three of them: `prefetch` (download), `vdb-validate` (check) and
`fasterq-dump` (convert to FASTQ). This chapter gets them working and
configured so they don't fill your home folder.

## Option 1: the Longleaf module

```bash
module avail sra          # find the module name and versions
module load sratoolkit    # use the name `module avail` shows; add /<version> to pin one
fasterq-dump --version
```

Use the newest 3.x version available. Older 2.x versions have bugs that
newer ones fix and lack some options.

## Option 2: conda (any Linux or Mac)

```bash
conda create -n sra -c conda-forge -c bioconda sra-tools pigz
conda activate sra
fasterq-dump --version
```

## Option 3: NCBI's prebuilt binaries

From the [SRA Toolkit install page](https://github.com/ncbi/sra-tools/wiki/02.-Installing-SRA-Toolkit):

```bash
## Linux (Ubuntu build; AlmaLinux build also available)
wget --output-document sratoolkit.tar.gz \
  https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra/sdk/current/sratoolkit.current-ubuntu64.tar.gz
## macOS
curl --output sratoolkit.tar.gz \
  https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra/sdk/current/sratoolkit.current-mac64.tar.gz

tar -vxzf sratoolkit.tar.gz
export PATH=$PWD/sratoolkit.3.*/bin:$PATH     # add to ~/.bashrc to keep it
which fasterq-dump
```

## Check it works

NCBI's own test fetches two reads from a small run and prints them:

```bash
fastq-dump --stdout -X 2 SRR390728
```

You should see eight lines of FASTQ. If it hangs or errors, see
[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).

## Configure it (once)

The toolkit keeps settings in `~/.ncbi/user-settings.mkfg`, edited with
`vdb-config`. Two things matter on a cluster.

### Where downloads go

Depending on configuration, `prefetch` saves into the **current
directory** or into a **user repository** (by default under your home, e.g.
`~/ncbi/public/sra`). Home on Longleaf is small, and a full home breaks
everything else. Choose the current directory, and always `cd` into
`/work` before downloading:

```bash
vdb-config --prefetch-to-cwd
```

(Or run `vdb-config -i`, open the **TOOLS** tab, and set the prefetch
location there.)

### SRA Lite or Normalized {#sra-lite-or-normalized}

`vdb-config -i` opens an interactive screen. On its main page there is an option
**"Prefer SRA Lite files with simplified base quality scores"**
([what that means](databases.qmd#whats-in-an-.sra-file)):

- **Unticked** (prefer Normalized, with full qualities): the safe choice when
  you'll look at quality plots or quality-trim.
- **Ticked**: smaller downloads, constant quality 30.

Navigate with the arrow keys or the highlighted letters, toggle with space,
and **Save** and **Exit** at the bottom.

::: {.callout-note}
## vdb-config on a fresh install

Newer toolkit versions may ask you to run `vdb-config -i` once before the
first download, even if you change nothing: open it, save, exit.
:::

## Where to run, and where to put the data

| Thing | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Downloads and conversion | `/work/users/<o>/<n>/<onyen>/...` | Large and fast; conversion needs lots of temporary space |
| Final `.fastq.gz` you'll keep | `/proj/<lab>/...` | Backed up; `/work` is purged |
| Commands | An interactive job or `sbatch` | Conversion is CPU- and disk-heavy: not on the login node |

```bash
srun -p interact -n 1 -c 6 --mem=8g -t 4:00:00 --pty bash   # interactive job with 6 CPUs
```
